newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BODARD IS BORDEAUX'S HERO IN PENALTY SHOOT-OUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BODARD IS BORDEAUX'S HERO IN PENALTY SHOOT-OUT.

text.p: Goalkeeper Gilbert Bodard saved three penalties then scored the winning spot-kick as Bordeaux reached the French League Cup final by beating Montpellier 7-6 in a shoot-out following a 2-2 draw after extra time on Tuesday.
The Belgian keeper made successive saves as the first three penalties in the shoot-out were all saved.
He then pounced on Montpellier's ninth penalty by Polish striker Roman Kosecki before beating his opposite number Philippe Flucklinger to put Bordeaux through.

Captain Patrick Colleter, who won the League Cup with Paris St Germain when it was first played two seasons ago, could have settled the issue sooner for Bordeaux. But he blasted his side's fifth penalty against the crossbar.
It was Bordeaux's second successive win on penalties in the competition after beating Caen at home in the quarter-finals.

Midfielder Stephane Ziani put Bordeaux in front four minutes into the second half of normal time when he weaved past two defenders and surprised Flucklinger with a low shot which the goalkeeper got an arm to but could not stop.
Montpellier equalised through Ivory Coast striker Ibrahim Bakayoko, whose low shot, half-parried by Bodard, trickled over the line just before it could be cleared by defender Bernard Lambourde.
The home side went ahead again in the sixth minute of extra time when striker Kaba Diawara was unchalleneged as he headed home a cross from the right by substitute Francois Grenet.
But Bordeaux, whose last trophies were the championship and French Cup double in 1987, gave away a second equaliser 11 minutes from the end.
The defence stood back for Laurent Robert's left-footed free kick from the right and Bodard was too late to reach the ball before it curled into the net at the far post.
